video_title: Zack McGuire: Dynamic Allocation and Concentrated Conviction at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta
gist: Zack McGuire, senior managing director at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta, details a capital-base-first, dynamic-allocation approach with a 30% defensive / 70% single-equity-bucket structure, thematic sleeves (tech, India, China, biotech), and conviction wins like adding to biotech when it crashed and a Japan activist manager now a top-three public position. He describes relationship-driven edges (GP stake purchase, discounted secondaries, insider-round venture access) and using the hospital system itself as a diligence and 'operating alpha' engine, while warning buyout may be getting crowded like hedge funds 15 years ago.

themes.theme: Capital base first: philosophy before allocation

insights.claim: McGuire argues institutional portfolios should be built starting from the nature of the capital base (liabilities, dependence on the portfolio, time horizon, governance, and both ability and willingness to take risk) rather than from asset allocation or manager selection.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Copying a peer endowment's allocation without its capital-base context is a structural error.
insights.quote: I don't like to start with asset allocation or manager selection. Where I like to start is what's the nature of the capital base that I'm working on behalf of.

insights.claim: An institution's ability to take risk and its willingness to take risk are distinct and must be assessed separately.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Risk budgets set on financial capacity alone can fail on governance/behavioral tolerance.
insights.quote: being able to understand the abilities both of the institutions's ability and willingness to take risk. And those are not the same thing.

insights.claim: Private equity funds and hedge funds are legal wrappers for strategies rather than asset classes in themselves, a view McGuire developed working across Emory, UGA Foundation and Maine PERS.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Allocators should analyze underlying exposures, not vehicle labels.
insights.quote: things like a private equity fund or hedge fund I mean those are those are rappers those are legal structures for different sort of investment strategies

insights.claim: At the small-team UGA Foundation, the team held a reasonable amount of passive exposure and concentrated staff time on hedge funds, private equity and venture capital, where return dispersion is greatest and access hardest.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Thin-staffed allocators should index the efficient sleeves and spend scarce hours where dispersion is widest.

insights.claim: Maine PERS has over 50% in alternatives, with infrastructure, real estate, resources, a healthy private credit allocation and significant co-investments used to help meet its discount rate, with less venture than a typical endowment.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Pensions use scale (co-invests, private credit) to hit actuarial targets differently than endowments with similar-looking allocations.

themes.theme: CHOA portfolio design: one equity bucket, dynamic allocation

insights.claim: Children's Healthcare of Atlanta runs a dual protection/performance mandate: about 30% in defensive, fixed-income-like, low-beta, low-equity-correlation assets and about 70% in a single equity bucket spanning public and private markets.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: A simplified two-bucket structure lets the team arbitrage public vs private equity on relative value.
insights.quote: about 30% of the assets are in what we call defensive or fixed income like uh assets

insights.claim: CHOA is explicitly indifferent between public and private equity, choosing whichever offers the best risk-adjusted return given market inefficiency or innovation, which McGuire says differs from how most institutions operate.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Removes the 'fill the bucket' pressure that pushes allocators into late-cycle private deployment.
insights.quote: we're actually indifferent between public or private equity and so that that's different than how most institutional investors pursue it.

insights.claim: The team practices dynamic rather than strategic asset allocation, pairing top-down diversification with bottom-up concentration and intensive manager selection.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Concentration happens at the manager level while risk is managed at the portfolio level.
insights.quote: the approach is one of dynamic asset allocation rather than strategic uh asset allocation

insights.claim: CHOA's stated strategy is to buy quality in public equity, build quality in private equity and back innovation in venture capital, overlaid with thematic allocations that have upper limits but no mandate to be filled.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Theme caps without fill mandates keep exposure dependent on finding exceptional managers.
insights.quote: buy quality and public equity, build quality and private equity and back innovation, venture capital.

insights.claim: Current CHOA themes include technology (public and private), India (mostly public plus limited VC), China public investments, and biotechnology (mostly public, with growing tech-bio exposure as life sciences and AI converge); themes are rewritten annually.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Signals where a sophisticated healthcare-system allocator sees inefficiency or innovation today.

insights.claim: The team is exploring but has not adopted new themes in Latin America (Brazil trip), Africa, and a commodities/energy/power super-cycle, where exposure is currently limited while it builds a top-down view and maps managers.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Early allocator interest in a commodities/power super-cycle could foreshadow institutional flows.
insights.quote: we're thinking deeply about commodities, energy, power, and super cycle. We have limited exposure today

insights.claim: A theme is investable when the market is healthy (reasonable rule of law, capital-market depth, little binary political risk), there is enough manager talent including an exceptional manager to express it, and a real pocket of innovation or inefficiency exists.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: A reusable three-part screen for emerging-market or thematic allocations.

insights.claim: About 35% of the CHOA portfolio in aggregate is invested in technology and healthcare-related investments.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Large tech/health weight gives the office both concentration risk and informational edge.
insights.quote: about 35% of the portfolio in aggregate is invested in technology and healthcare related investments.

insights.claim: Board reporting focuses on top-down portfolio beta, liquidity (including uncalled committed capital), number of managers and manager concentration, rather than on filling asset-class buckets, though every line item is disclosed.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: A governance template for flexible mandates that keeps committees focused on risk, not labels.

themes.theme: Conviction calls: biotech, Japan activism, buyout crowding

insights.claim: When biotech crashed after strong performance, CHOA rewrote the theme, kept conviction in its managers, and added capital while it was down; that sleeve became by far the best-compounding segment of its public equity portfolio.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Adding to a drawn-down theme with conviction in managers paid off; supports contrarian rebalancing into biotech.
insights.quote: the level of compounding within that portfolio was by far the best performing public equity segment and so we stuck through added capital when it was down.

insights.claim: In 2023 the team concluded that an aggressive corporate activist manager was the best way to express Japan's corporate governance reforms; it has compounded tremendously, is now the third-largest position in CHOA's public equity portfolio, and is earning buyout-like returns or better.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Japan governance-reform activism delivered private-equity-like returns in liquid form.
insights.quote: really decided that um an aggressive corporate activist manager was the best way uh to express that

insights.claim: McGuire suggests buyout may be going through what hedge funds experienced about 15 years ago, with heavy capital inflows squeezing out alpha, which is why CHOA focuses on the lower middle market.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Expect compressing buyout alpha outside the lower middle market; favor small, nimble managers.
insights.quote: I think maybe buyout as an asset class is possibly going through what what hedge funds went through 15 years ago where you had so much capital come into the space a lot of that alpha squeeze out.

insights.claim: McGuire describes a pre-ChatGPT (2021-2022) software fund commitment that may not turn out well because the dynamic changed, and he does not classify it as a mistake since it was unforeseeable through diligence.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Vintage 2021-22 software private funds face AI-driven disruption risk LPs are already acknowledging.
insights.quote: I thought about around like maybe a software investment that I made a few years ago and right that was pre-Chat GBT and that may not turn out to be a great fund

insights.claim: McGuire's own avoidable investment mistakes have most often stemmed from misreading people: GP motivation, economic alignment and ability to attract and retain talent.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Diligence time is best spent on people and alignment, not just strategy.

insights.claim: He prefers newer firms in some cases because managers focused on generating wealth are better aligned than those preserving wealth already accumulated, and argues a consensus portfolio resembling the benchmark cannot produce alpha.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Emerging-manager risk can be an alignment advantage.
insights.quote: if we have a consensus portfolio that looks like our benchmark, we can't produce alpha, right?

themes.theme: Venture access and the 'full life cycle' LP edge

insights.claim: Only two of the venture managers in CHOA's portfolio when McGuire joined remain; the team rebuilt what he calls a world-class VC portfolio by evangelizing the hospital mission, getting on planes (he went to California nine times last year), and joining ecosystem nodes that then generate referrals.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Mission-driven LPs can win access to capacity-constrained VC through persistence and network referrals.

insights.claim: CHOA's venture core is now built, so its aspirational manager list is much smaller than three years ago, and it is willing to back first-time funds but not first-time investors.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Emerging-manager risk is taken on fund structure, not on unproven investing talent.
insights.quote: We don't want to invest in first- time with first- time investors, per se

insights.claim: The office is transitioning from deployment to optimization: marketable portfolio is now one-in-one-out, and privates have gone from adding a handful of new managers a year to zero to two.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Fully invested allocators raise the bar; new GPs must be additive or upgrades.

insights.claim: CHOA co-led with another health care system the purchase of a 10% stake in an existing manager's management company to fund founder succession and growth, a GP-stakes deal sourced through 10-15 years of LP relationship.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Long-tenured LPs can access proprietary GP-stakes deals competing with dedicated GP-stakes firms.
insights.quote: between the two of us to buy 10% in this management company of this this manager.

insights.claim: Through a manager-guided secondary, CHOA bought what it considers a high-quality asset at a significant discount that was highly accretive on day one.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Relationship-driven secondaries are a source of day-one alpha for trusted LPs.

insights.claim: McGuire observes that venture has split into two markets, insider rounds and primary rounds, and CHOA is backing a trusted advisor firm that receives equity from companies, letting CHOA access deals often at insider-round prices.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Insider-round pricing is a distinct, cheaper venture market that creative LP structures can tap.
insights.quote: there's almost like two venture markets that have evolved and so there's the insider round and then there's the the the the primary round

insights.claim: McGuire frames compounding relationships with highest-conviction partners as one of the best ways to compound capital, via co-invest first calls, secondaries, GP stakes and proprietary deals.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Being an exceptional LP is itself an alpha source.
insights.quote: one of the best ways to compound children's capital. It's a compound of relationships with our best and highest conviction partners.

themes.theme: Operating alpha: hospital system as diligence edge

insights.claim: CHOA created a healthcare advisory committee about two years ago to channel portfolio access to investors, companies, regulators and experts into 'operating alpha' for the hospital system, and in reverse lets managers test company ideas with CHOA clinicians.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Healthcare-system LPs have a proprietary customer-validation channel for health-tech diligence.

insights.claim: McGuire passed on an attractive passive health-tech co-investment after CHOA clinical and technology leaders said the system was unlikely to pay for an enterprise version, especially given the high valuation.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Buyer-side validation from a leading pediatric system can kill richly valued health-AI deals.
insights.quote: I probably should pass on this one given high valuation.

insights.claim: CHOA hosted an AI-in-the-healthcare-enterprise symposium featuring Thrive Capital's Dr. Nora Aayogu (as transcribed) and plans a spring life-sciences version, positioning the office as a convening node between health systems and AI investors.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: Health systems are actively shaping AI adoption priorities that VCs care about.

insights.claim: McGuire advises young allocators that as AI makes analysis more efficient, their unique contribution shifts to judgment, accountability and portfolio-level perspective, best developed through mentorship.
insights.speaker: Zack McGuire
insights.so_what: AI commoditizes analyst work in allocator offices; judgment becomes the scarce skill.
insights.quote: AI is an accelerant for those things but it's really how do you develop judgment
